text:
Jake Sanderson has played 16 games for Ottawa and is already logging 23:17 a night, the minutes of a team's top defenseman. His return was a big enough deal that Graeme Nichols of Coming Down the Pipe wrote a full analytics piece on what it changed. At five-on-five the Senators have taken 54.7% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice.

The points are coming the patient way: 13 in 16 games, 12 of them assists, and seven assists in his last ten with no goal. One goal on 2.48 expected and a 3.3% shooting rate is low even for a pass-first defenseman; our range for his true rate runs 5.4% to 9%. Some of those shots should start going in.

None of this is new. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 3.3 wins above replacement in 2025-26, fifth among 215 defensemen, much of it on the power play, plus 3.2 goals from drawing more penalties than he takes. NHL Edge puts his top skating speed in the 99th percentile. Our numbers project 57 points (range 46 to 69), and the players he most resembles are Charlie McAvoy, Roman Josi and Miro Heiskanen.
headline: Sanderson keeps feeding Ottawa, still waiting on goals
